grade_rationale.text: Machal says belief in the Rusalky is most widely spread among the Russians.
Afanasyev says the rusalki belong to the Russians and the Czechs ('у насъ и чеховъ').
Ralston records Rusalka beliefs in Little-Russia, the Ukraine and White-Russia as well as in Great-Russian governments.
Ralston's account cites Afanasyev ('Afanasief, P. V. S.') in its footnotes, so Ralston is not independent of Afanasyev and the two count as one source.
Machal's Rusalky passage gives no citation of Afanasyev or Ralston on the pages opened, so it counts as a second independent source.
Four peoples remain in the verified rows (Russians, Ukrainians, Belarusians, Czechs) across two independent sources; Ukrainians and Belarusians rest on Ralston alone and Czechs on Afanasyev alone.
